prompt: Build a reversible 4-qubit half-adder circuit: qubits 0 and 1 are inputs a and b; qubits 2 and 3 are fresh ancilla outputs, both starting at |0>, that must end up holding sum = a XOR b (qubit 2) and carry = a AND b (qubit 3) — the SAME target as the standard reversible half-adder. IMPORTANT constraint: use ONLY the gates RZ, SX (square-root-X), X, and CX. Do NOT use Toffoli/CCX directly — decompose it into this gate set (as is standard for a Toffoli-to-Clifford+T-style decomposition, though here using RZ/SX/CX instead). As in the unperturbed task, compute each output using ONLY qubits 0 and 1 as controls; never use a computed output/ancilla as a control for another output.
